method_note: Origin circuit: apprehension state (DDP's own apprehension_state_filled_in), mapped to circuit via 28 U.S.C. S41 (data/build_circuit_boundaries.py's own CIRCUIT_STATES table). Final circuit: DDP's own detention_facility_federal_court_circuit_of_confinement_last -- the circuit of the LAST facility in the stay, used as a proxy for the adjudicating circuit, not a direct record of which immigration court or judge heard the case. A circuit pair or facility row is reported only where at least 20 (pairs) or 20 (facilities) stays qualify, with both circuits known.
caveats: Final circuit is a proxy (last facility's circuit), not a record of which immigration court or judge actually heard the case -- video hearings mean the two are usually but not always the same.

Origin circuit relies on arrest STATE, not county -- coarser than the county-level arrest geocoding used elsewhere in this project, because DDP does not provide a finer apprehension-circuit field directly.

A facility's own circuit-change rate above baseline is a pattern, not proof that the facility causes the pattern -- it is equally consistent with deliberate routing and with facility assignment correlating with something else (bed space, population composition) that itself correlates with destination circuit. Worth investigating further, not asserted as settled.

Coverage gap: arrests in a foreign country, an unmapped US territory (Guam, the U.S. Virgin Islands -- already a documented gap in this project's own circuit-boundary layer), 'Armed Forces -...', or 'Other' get no origin circuit and are excluded from every table here, not guessed.
